chapter: Regal Theatre, bebop and the Woody Herman date
title: Why Woody Herman hired Ben Webster, Hodges and Tizol for the 1944 date
summary: Saunders explains that Woody wanted star soloists for his records because good musicians were scarce and his Herds were just beginning, with Ben Webster's solo on The Music Stopped.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Red, that date that we talked about last week, with Woody Herman, Juan Tizol, Ben Webster and Johnny Hodges and you, and -- what was that, about 1943, '44?
This were during the war, yeah, right, during the war years. I think it had to be about '44, around '43 or '44. [un. p 56.]
How did that come about? What -- that was an out of the ordinary thing for Woody to do.

Well, it was out of the ordinary because musicians at that time are really scarce, good musicians, and Woody had a good band, but he wanted extra -- something extra for the records, because he had put out all of these -- "Apple Honey and things -- I mean, not Apple Honey at that time, before Apple Honey, but he had been recording all of these things, and he'd had terrific men, and he wanted this particular sound in a soloist. And one of the tunes was "The Music Stopped," do you remember that, with -- Ben Webster played a beautiful solo on that.
But he wanted this particular sound and he wanted his band, because this was the time he was beginning to come out of his -- the things that he had made.
A sort of Dixie -- a big Dixieland --

Right. So now he wanted to get this wild sound and then the Herds were just beginning and this type of a thing. So this is why, because he didn't have the adequate men at that particular time, soloists. So this is really the reason for them being in the band.
That was really an all-star date. Not too many people know about that date, either.

That's right, right, well, it was kind of smothered because the Army -- and a lot of things went on, juggling the men and things like that, and men went from band to band during those days, and not too much was known about it. Because --
